author: m. a. zimmerman
title: Adam Smith questions U.S.-Iran conflict and comments on G.I. Bill legacy
text:
Rep. Adam Smith, U.S. Congressman representing Washington’s 9th district since 1997, posted a series of statements on June 23, 2026, reflecting on military benefits, the aftermath of war with Iran, and actions by former President Donald Trump.
In his first post on June 23 at 02:14 UTC, Smith wrote: “Since the G.I. Bill was passed 82 years ago, 15 million men and women in the armed forces have had the opportunity to seek higher education, rather than unemployment following their military service. I look forward to seeing the many opportunities that the G.I. Bill brings to”.
Later that day at 15:18 UTC, he questioned recent foreign policy decisions regarding Iran: “What did all of the lives lost and disruption to the global economy accomplish? We should not have started the war with Iran just to be back to where we were before the conflict started.”
At 18:01 UTC on June 23, Smith commented on domestic politics: “Donald Trump continues to use the U.S. government to go after his political enemies.”
Smith has been a consistent presence in Congress since replacing Randy Tate in Washington’s 9th district nearly three decades ago. He previously served in the Washington State Senate from 1991 until joining Congress in 1997. Born in Washington D.C. in 1965 and now residing in Bellevue at age 57, Smith holds a BA from Fordham University (1987) and a JD from the University of Washington (1990).
